cards.text: Elisha the prophet calls over one of the sons of the prophets and hands him a job. Tuck your cloak under your belt, take this flask of oil, and go to Ramoth-gilead. Friend, I don't know what that oil's for yet, but nobody tucks up their cloak to walk SLOW.

cards.question: Elisha tells the young man who to look for once he gets to Ramoth-gilead. Who is it?

cards.text: Elisha says to go in and get Jehu away from his companions. Whatever this is, friend, it is NOT a group announcement.

cards.question: Once the young prophet gets Jehu away from his companions, where does Elisha tell him to take Jehu?

cards.text: Then the flask comes out: Elisha says pour the oil right on Jehu's head and speak the LORD's words. Pour oil on an army commander's HEAD? Friend, I won't even tap a stranger on the shoulder to tell him his apron's untied.

cards.question: Elisha says that with the oil on Jehu's head, the young prophet is to speak for the LORD and say He anoints Jehu ___ over Israel.
Elisha tells the young prophet that once he anoints Jehu, he should stay and wait for Jehu's answer.

cards.text: So the young prophet heads to Ramoth-gilead and walks in on the army commanders, all sitting there together. He says he has a message for the commander, which is like walking into a room FULL of managers and asking to speak to the manager.

cards.question: When the young prophet says he has a message for the commander, Jehu asks which of them it's for.

cards.text: "For you, commander," comes the answer, so Jehu gets up and follows him into the house.

There the oil goes on Jehu's head with the LORD's word: "I anoint you king over the LORD’s people Israel." Friend, Jehu didn't apply, didn't interview, didn't even get a heads-up, and he just got the BIGGEST promotion in the country.

cards.question: The LORD gives Jehu a job: strike down the house of his master. Whose house is it?
What reason does the LORD give Jehu for striking down Ahab's house?

answers.text: To avenge the blood of His prophets
To win back the land from Aram
To give Israel a stronger army

cards.text: Ahab was king of Israel (1 Kings 16:29), and Jezebel was his wife (1 Kings 16:31). The LORD says His servants' blood was shed by Jezebel's hand.

cards.question: The LORD keeps speaking to Jehu about Ahab's house. How much of it does He say will perish?

cards.text: The LORD says He'll make Ahab's house like the houses of Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah. Those were earlier kings of Israel, and each one's whole house was struck down (1 Kings 15:29; 16:11).

cards.question: The LORD says someone will give Jezebel a proper burial.

cards.text: On the plot of ground at Jezreel the dogs will devour her, and there will be no one to bury her. Then the young prophet opens the door and RUNS, just like Elisha said, and I respect a man who follows instructions all the way out the door.

Jehu walks back out to his master's servants, and they want to know if everything's all right, and why this madman came to him. Madman. That's what they're calling the guy who just made their commander KING.

cards.question: When the servants ask why the madman came, how does Jehu answer them at first?

answers.text: He brushes it off as prophet babble
He says the man had the wrong commander
He says the man came asking for money

cards.text: The servants aren't buying it. They fire right back: "That is a lie!" and "Tell us now!" That's the exact look I get when I swear I only tasted ONE cookie.

cards.question: With the servants pushing him, what does Jehu finally tell them?

answers.text: The LORD anointed him king over Israel
The prophet brought news of a battle
Elisha wants to meet with him soon

cards.question: Quickly, each man takes his ___ and puts it under Jehu on the bare steps.
Right there on the steps, the men blow the ram's horn and proclaim Jehu king.

cards.text: One minute Jehu's sitting in a meeting, the next there's a pile of garments under him and a ram's horn blowing for him. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Then the flask comes out...', 'Pour oil on an army commander's HEAD?' and 'Friend, I won't even tap a stranger...'. Only the opening card may run to 3.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Ahab is first named on card 12, as the answer, and again in this card's question. He isn't said to be king of Israel until card 14, after both questions. Once card 12 is answered, the next card can say who he is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The right answer, 'To avenge the blood of His prophets', sounds like Scripture and is the only spiritual reason. Both wrong answers, about Aram and a stronger army, are military, so the right answer stands out. No story card sets up the prophets' blood either.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card is only flat reference facts ('Ahab was king of Israel... Jezebel was his wife...'). It has none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card is two dry reference sentences about Jeroboam and Baasha. It has none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Jehu walks back out...', 'Madman.' and 'That's what they're calling...'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'the guy who just made their commander KING' says the young prophet made Jehu king. In the text, the LORD says 'I anoint you king' (2 Kings 9:6). It also calls Jehu the servants' commander, but the text calls them 'the servants of his master' (9:11).

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'The servants aren't buying it.', 'They fire right back...' and 'That's the exact look I get...'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The first sentence retells verse 13 (the garments and the ram's horn), which cards 9 and 10 already asked. Since the last verse is asked on a choice card, this card should be only the story-continues line.
The story-continues line, 'And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this story is NOT done', nearly copies the doc's example line instead of being a new one.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
